messages:
eve: Velociti sent RFI back; flagged three exceptions they want answered this week: customer HSM for Private, FedRAMP for Dedicated, and how caching changes billing.
mark: Copying their exact asks so we map answers: 
> HSM: Can customers bring/attach their own HSM to Private?
> FedRAMP: Any Redwood offering FedRAMP-authorized?
> Billing: How does prefix/KV caching affect token billing and what are per-token vs per-request rules?
tara: Quick factual bullets to draft replies: Private/on-prem can be configured to use customer HSM appliances and customer-managed cloud KMS. Dedicated supports cloud KMS integrations (customer keys). Hosted multitenant does not accept customer HSM hardware.
sam: FedRAMP status: Not authorized as of 2026-03-20. We have a compliance roadmap and partner-assisted options for regulated deployments; direct FedRAMP pursuit is possible for high-priority engagements.
security: For the questionnaire I'll attach vendor list: AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, GCP KMS, Thales Luna, Utimaco. Marked validated for Private: AWS KMS, Thales Luna.
tara: Billing summary draft: Hosted = per-token; Dedicated = committed capacity (monthly) + overage per-token. Prefix/KV cache reduces billed tokens on hit; typical chat workloads see ~25-40% reduction depending on prompt shape. I'll add a worked example with placeholders.
mark: I'll assemble capability_matrix.csv (cols: capability,hosted,dedicated,private,notes) and include a row for Customer HSM = no,partial,yes with note explaining differences.
eve: Ops-bot reminder and AE sign-off request please. Target upload Thu 16:30 PT so AE can review.
ops-bot: Reminder created: Velociti RFI bundle due 2026-03-26 17:00 PT. Required attachments: capability_matrix.csv, security_questionnaire_filled.pdf, hsm_diagram.png, pricing_estimate.xlsx. Notifying @eve and @mark.
